newsitem.title: USA: Bema wants entire Arizona Star for sale.
newsitem.headline: Bema wants entire Arizona Star for sale.

text.p: Bema Gold Corp chairman, president and chief executive officer Clive Johnson said that absent a bid for the entire company, it would not sell its 33 percent stake in Arizona Star Resource Corp.
Johnson made his comments at the American Stock Exchange's 1997 Gold Conference in response to earlier reports that the company would sell its interest in Arizona Star.

Johnson said the sale of Arizona Star to a major mining company is its preferred option for attracting a developer for its $1 billion Cerro Casale project in Chile. Johnson said he preferred the sale of all of Arizona Star to a major mining company because it would be the simplest means to attract a developer. Arizona Star owns 51 percent of Cerro Casale and Bema owns 49 percent
Building the Cerro Casale mine itself would take resources away from Bema's other projects, he said.
However, Johnson would not rule out the option of bringing in a major partner, including a copper producer, to forestall the sale of Arizona Star and having the new partner invest in the development.
Cerro Casale, which is believed to be the largest undeveloped gold project in the world, contains an estimated 24.8 million ounces of gold and 6.4 billion pounds of copper.
Earlier today, a company spokesman said 20 companies are investigating Cerro Casale and tests performed by one of the companies showed results comparable to Bema's expectations.
Cerro Casale is believed to be the largest undeveloped gold project in the world since Bre-X Minerals Ltd's BXM.TO claims about the Busang project in Indonesia were found to be false, Johnson said.
"We're seeing a lot more due diligence on the front end of these projects since Bre-X," Johnson said.
